newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline slightly weaker under selling pressure.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline slightly weaker under selling pressure.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices were slightly weaker on Tuesday with very limited transatlantic arbitrage options drawing fresh cargo selling interest and pegging back Rotterdam barge prices, traders said.

On the key Rotterdam barge market running refinery material was trading $3 under Monday's opening levels at $187 with prompt ARA liftings offered at a relatively stable $185, closing the gap between the two markets from $4 to around $2 a tonne.
Early July Rotterdam liftings were also on offer at $186 but drew little buying interest.
Traders said the combination of lengthy supplies in the ARA region and the steep backwardation of around $3-4 to July was keeping buying interest thin.
July and August swaps were valued around $181.50 a tonne.

High stocks and high refinery runs in the U.S. were seen limiting arbitrage options for a while. This saw cargo prices for Eurograde gasoline marked around $1 per tonne lower to $187/$189 cif NWE but traders said the wide range reflected relaxed demand.
